title: Three Thousand Tons of Syrup Vanished From a Maple Syrup Warehouse
hook: An inspector climbing onto a syrup barrel nearly fell. The barrel was empty

open.title: A syrup inspector nearly stumbled, and the barrel was to blame
open.line: A syrup warehouse in Quebec, Canada. During the yearly inventory check, an inspector staggered while climbing onto a barrel. Something was off with it.

summary: From 2011 to 2012, nearly three thousand tons of syrup were secretly drained from a maple syrup reserve warehouse in Quebec. Some barrels held water instead of syrup.

text: July 2012, a syrup warehouse in Quebec, Canada.
An inspector climbing the barrels nearly fell.
A full barrel weighs about 600 pounds.
But stepping on it showed it was empty.

panels.text: Where did all the syrup go?

text: The Quebec producers' federation stockpiled syrup here.
It stores extra in good years and releases it in bad to steady prices.
Producers gave 25% of their harvest to the reserve.
It then handled 77% of the world's maple syrup supply.
Actually, thieves drained syrup from barrels for months.
Some held water instead of syrup.
Shipped to Vermont (US) and New Brunswick (Canada), it sold in small batches.
Nearly three thousand tons were gone, worth C$18.7 million.
Per Canada's Supreme Court, police arrested 16 people.
The ringleader got 8 years and a fine over 9 million dollars, upheld in 2022.
